summary: Iter95 — Live e2e backend validation of the Negotiation state machine + Tier pricing + Payment gating. 37 of 38 new live tests pass (plus all 25 pre-existing iter92/92b/93 import/static tests). One CRITICAL gap confirmed: GET /api/sessions/{id} does not surface negotiation fields, and a SECOND CRITICAL gap confirmed by code review: POST /api/payments/create-payment-intent has NO server-side gate on paymentReady/negotiationStatus — the only reason it currently returns 400 pre-agreement is an UNRELATED expired Stripe key, NOT a gate. All other flows (propose/counter/accept/reject/timeline, permissions, turn-enforcement, expiry, pricing quote, admin tier assignment) work as specified.

critical.issue: Response does NOT include negotiationStatus, agreedTime, agreedLocation, paymentReady. SessionResponse pydantic model at /app/backend/models.py:402 is missing these four fields, so even though the DB stores them, the API strips them. The frontend payment screen / session-detail screen will not see negotiation state via /api/sessions/{id} and must fall back to the negotiation/timeline endpoint.

Endpoint at /app/backend/routes/payment_routes.py:908-927 has ZERO server-side gating on paymentReady / negotiationStatus=='agreed'. It only validates amount bounds (100<=amount<=500000) then calls Stripe. Any authenticated user can create a payment intent for any session_id (or no session_id) regardless of negotiation state. The auto-test 'create_payment_intent_blocked_before_agreed' superficially passes only because the live Stripe key is expired and returns 400; with a valid Stripe key the endpoint would happily charge before both parties agree. Must add: load session by session_id, require session.paymentReady is True AND current_user is the trainee on that session, else 400/403.

minor.issue: Live Stripe secret key (sk_live_...QtF7) is expired in the backend environment — even legitimate payment flows return 400 'Expired API Key'. Unrelated to negotiation but blocks any post-agreement payment e2e validation.

action_items: Add negotiationStatus, agreedTime, agreedLocation, paymentReady to SessionResponse in /app/backend/models.py (line ~402) and ensure /api/sessions/{id} populates them from the session doc.

Add payment-gate logic to POST /api/payments/create-payment-intent in /app/backend/routes/payment_routes.py:908: if session_id provided, load session, verify current_user is the trainee on that session, and verify session.paymentReady is True / negotiationStatus == 'agreed' — else raise HTTPException(400, 'Negotiation not yet agreed').
Rotate the expired Stripe secret key in backend/.env so payment intent creation can succeed in tests post-agreement.
(Cosmetic) GET /api/sessions/{id}/negotiation/timeline still includes a hard-to-read expiresInMinutes expression (lines 321-328 of negotiation_routes.py) — works, but worth refactoring for clarity.
critical_code_review_comments: negotiation_routes.py: state machine is clean, well-documented, and behaves exactly per spec (proposed→counter→accept→agreed; reject→rejected→re-propose; expiry after 60min). All 7 endpoint behaviours pass live e2e.
pricing_tiers.py: canonical pricing matches frontend mirror; calculate_pricing invariants hold (take_home+commission=base; customer_total=base+fee).

payment_routes.py:908 create_payment_intent — MISSING SECURITY/GATING CHECK. session_id is accepted as a query param but never used to verify negotiation state or even that the session belongs to the caller. This contradicts the entire iter93/94 negotiation contract.

models.py:402 SessionResponse — fields list is hard-coded and was not extended when iter93 added negotiationStatus/agreedTime/agreedLocation/paymentReady. Consider switching to `model_config = ConfigDict(extra='allow')` or adding the new fields explicitly.
negotiation_routes.py: timeline endpoint correctly auto-expires stale proposals on read — verified live by back-dating negotiationLastUpdatedAt 2h then GETting timeline.

context_for_next_testing_agent: After main agent (a) extends SessionResponse with the 4 negotiation fields and (b) adds the paymentReady gate to /api/payments/create-payment-intent, re-run `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iteration95_negotiation_e2e.py -v` and expect 16/16 to pass. The TestPaymentGating.test_create_payment_intent_blocked_before_agreed assertion accepts 400/402/403/409 — once the gate is added, the response code can be 400 with a 'negotiation' / 'agree' / 'paymentReady' detail string and the test will still pass. Note: a valid Stripe key is also needed for the post-agreement test to truly exercise Stripe; the current test already permits Stripe-side failures as long as the failure detail does NOT mention gating.
rca of the issue: Both critical gaps stem from the iter93 negotiation feature being wired only at the routes/negotiation_routes.py boundary without propagating the new contract into (a) the session response schema and (b) the payment intent route. SessionResponse predates iter93 and was never extended; create_payment_intent predates the negotiation gate concept entirely. Mitigation is small and surgical: add 4 Optional fields to SessionResponse, and add ~10 lines of gate logic (load session, verify trainee + paymentReady) at the top of create_payment_intent.
